## Validation — builds [#90228](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90228), [#90261](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90261), baseline [#90243](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90243)

Commit `a287ff6444` (`refs/pull/57965/head`, on `main` 8b98b7d0b4). Scoped to `lm-eval-large-models-8xh200` + `amd-lm-eval-large-models-8xh200`. Two validation runs, both green: all 5 shards + the mirror passed on the first attempt, no empty shards. Coverage reconciles exactly with the unsharded baseline: 6/6 configs pass on the primary lane; the mirror lane runs 3 passed / 5 platform-skipped, identical to main. 90228's numbers were polluted by cold weight caches on first-touch nodes; 90261 (warm) is the cleaner measurement and agrees with 90228 on the structural overhead below.

Measured per replica, 90261 (`pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause`):

| shard | config | pytest | wall | overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 0 | DeepSeek-R1-TP | 17.2m | 18.0m | 0.8m | container start |
| 1 | DeepSeek-R1-DP | 17.6m | 18.4m | 0.8m | container start |
| 2 | DeepSeek-V3.2-TP | 20.2m | 21.0m | 0.8m | container start |
| 3 | DeepSeek-V3.2-DP | 18.2m | 19.0m | 0.8m | container start |
| 4 | Nemotron-3-Super BF16+FP8 | 13.3m | 14.1m | 0.8m | container start |
| mirror | models-mi3xx list | 16.8m | 21.9m | 5.1m | image pull + ROCm setup |

- Baseline (same-day, unsharded, build 90243 on `main`): 69.7m pytest / 70.7m wall. `W_after` = 90.5m → **+19.8 extra worker-minutes vs the ≤20 budget** (passes, with no headroom).
- Slowest replica: 20.2m pytest (shard 2) — **0.2m over the 20m target**; historical worst for that config is 13.2m (prediction was ≤18.6m). Rationale for 5 shards stands: any pairing of the four large configs exceeds 20m (e.g. DeepSeek-V3.2-TP + -DP would be ~31m), and a single config's runtime cannot be reduced by adding replicas.
- **Where the extra ~20m goes (fully attributed):** DeepGEMM JIT warmup is cached per container. The unsharded job pays it 5.0/2.0/0/0m across its four sequential DeepSeek configs; sharded, every DeepSeek shard pays a cold 4–5m (measured 5.0/5.0/4.0/4.0) — ≈ +11m of repeated compilation. The rest is 4 extra container starts (≈ +3m) and per-config weight loads no longer benefiting from the previous config's page cache (R1-DP +2.6m, V3.2-DP +6.2m on 90261; same-day baseline on the same agent shows 12.6m/9.4m startups vs 15.2m/15.6m sharded).
- Mirror lane: unchanged command, pinned to `parallelism: 1`; 16.8m pytest is inside its own recent unsharded range (15.2–17.7m), well under its 65m timeout.
- The ~5m first-case DeepGEMM warmup is also paid by the unsharded job on every run — a shared/persistent JIT cache for these jobs would save more than this PR's entire overhead; happy to file that as a follow-up if there's interest.

**Verdict:** aggregate cost is within budget (+19.8 of 20); the slowest-shard target is marginally exceeded (20.2m vs 20m) solely because of the repeated per-shard DeepGEMM warmup. Requesting an explicit ruling on that 0.2m overage rather than relaxing the target silently — the alternatives (4 shards, or pairing configs) all put a shard past 23m.

## Validation — build [#90304](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90304) (named per-model jobs)

Commit `73577f84c6` (`refs/pull/57965/head`, rebased onto `main` 382970ee6c). Scoped to the five new jobs + `amd-lm-eval-large-models`. **All six passed on the first attempt** — no retries, no empty selections. Coverage reconciles exactly with the unsharded baseline: each named job ran its expected config(s) and only those (1 passed per DeepSeek job, 2 passed for Nemotron, mirror 3 passed / 5 platform-skipped — identical to main).

Measured per job (`pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause`):

| job | pytest | wall | overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| DeepSeek R1 TP | 18.2m | 20.4m | 2.2m | container start + image pull |
| DeepSeek R1 DP | 18.6m | 20.9m | 2.3m | container start + image pull |
| DeepSeek V3.2 TP | 20.4m | 21.2m | 0.8m | container start |
| DeepSeek V3.2 DP | 18.4m | 20.7m | 2.3m | container start + image pull |
| Nemotron 3 Super | 12.6m | 13.5m | 0.9m | container start |
| (MI300) LM Eval Large Models | 15.2m | 22.5m | 7.3m | image pull + ROCm setup |

- Baseline (same-day unsharded, build 90243 on `main`): 69.7m pytest / 70.7m wall → Σwall 96.7m, **+26.0 extra worker-minutes this run** (+19.8 on the earlier identical-workload run 90261; run-to-run swing is pool/load-dependent). The structural, layout-inherent part is ≈ +14m: per-job DeepGEMM JIT warmup (the unsharded job amortizes it 5/2/0/0m across the four sequential DeepSeek configs; each named job pays a cold 4–5m) plus four repeated container setups.
- Slowest job: DeepSeek V3.2 TP at 20.4m pytest — 0.4m over the 20m target on this run (18.6m worst in the pre-split history; the overage is the cold DeepGEMM warmup, same finding as the first validation).
- Mirror lane unchanged in behavior: 15.2m pytest, inside its own recent range (15.2–17.7m), far under its 65m timeout.
- Same request as on the shard-layout validation: the runtime target is marginally exceeded only because of the repeated per-job DeepGEMM warmup. A shared/persistent JIT cache for these eval jobs would recover ~11m of the overhead (and ~7m/run on today's unsharded main job) — happy to file that as a follow-up.
